item.title: Radio-frequency electron cascade in semiconductor quantum dots
item.description:
Pay dirt new method — Dispersive rf electron-cascade readout enhances signal-to-noise ratio over direct in-situ sensing, yielding lower-bound amplitude SNR gains of A≈50 and A≈40 in two silicon quantum dot architectures.

Grade 0.502 · 2.9σ above the day's baseline · matched “Semiconductor spin qubits” · Tara Murphy, Lorenzo Peri, Giovanni A. Oakes, Jacob F. Chittock-Wood, Ross C. C. Leon, Fabrizio Berritta, Amber Heskes, David Wise, Anasua Chatterjee, Ferdinand Kuemmeth, M. Fernando Gonzalez-Zalba

Figure

Calculated cascade power-response gain A versus drive amplitude, lever-arm ratio, and temperature over tunnel coupling. Shows transition between linear-response gain scaling A∝r−4(Δ/kBT)2 and large-drive saturation A∝r−2.

Asks

How can high-frequency cotunneling cascades amplify dispersive reflectometry readout signals in semiconductor quantum-dot arrays?

But

Requires adding a sensor dot tuned to charge degeneracy; susceptible to charge drift and finite-frequency effects.

Tools

rf reflectometry · silicon metal-oxide-semiconductor (SiMOS) quantum dot device · fully depleted silicon-on-insulator (FDSOI) quantum dot array · RF-Squad electrostatic simulator

Abstract

Electron cotunneling in semiconductor quantum dots is a higher-order tunneling mechanism that connects initial and final charge states through energetically inaccessible virtual intermediate configurations. In quantum-dot arrays, such processes can produce simultaneous charge motion across multiple tunnel junctions and enable transitions that would otherwise be suppressed by Coulomb blockade. Here, building on an earlier proof-of-principle demonstration, we investigate radio-frequency (rf)-driven correlated cotunneling and its application to dispersive quantum-dot readout. Using both theoretical modeling and experimental measurements in two different foundry-fabricated silicon devices, we show that an external rf drive can induce correlated cyclic single-electron transitions, resulting in enhanced charge-polarization of the system. We develop a general theoretical framework for rf electron-cascade readout, which exploits cotunneling events in quantum-dot systems with three or more dots to produce a relative signal enhancement, and extend its experimental demonstration to a gate-sensed device architecture. Our results establish the operating principles of rf electron-cascade readout and provide a route to increased dispersive readout fidelity in semiconductor quantum computing architectures.

item.title: Epitaxial NbN-junction-based self-shunted superconducting flux qubit with high anharmonicity
item.description:
Pay dirt new result — Epitaxial NbN/AlN/NbN self-shunted flux qubit achieves anharmonicity of 797 MHz with lifetime T1 of 13 to 25 μs without external shunt capacitor.

Grade 0.469 · 2.5σ above the day's baseline · matched “Superconducting Qubits: Current State of Play” · Tokunoshin Uchida, Shingo Nozaki, Daiki Kurihara, Hiroki Kutsuma, Shotaro Shirai, Atsushi Noguchi, Hirotaka Terai, Taro Yamashita

Asks

Can full epitaxially grown NbN/AlN/NbN junctions realize an ultracompact, highly anharmonic self-shunted flux qubit with long coherence times?

Before

Conventional NbN-based C-shunt flux qubits require large shunt capacitors, and typical Al-based flux qubits with comparable coherence use junction areas more than 10 times smaller.

But

Measured coherence lifetimes restricted to 13 to 25 μs regime.

Tools

Epitaxial NbN/AlN/NbN Josephson junctions · Self-shunted superconducting flux qubit (SSFQ) · Dispersive readout setup

Abstract

We report a demonstration of a self-shunted superconducting flux qubit (SSFQ) as an ultracompact, strongly anharmonic, and long-lifetime qubit by using the full epitaxially grown NbN/AlN/NbN Josephson junctions. The NbN-junction-based SSFQ achieved a high anharmonicity of 797 MHz as well as drastically reduced footprint of the qubit compared to capacitively shunted (C-shunt) flux qubits with a large shunt capacitor. The lifetime of the SSFQ reached 13 - 25 μs, which is comparable to or relatively higher than that of NbN-based C-shunt flux qubits and Al-based flux qubits with more than 10 times smaller junctions. This indicates that the large epitaxial NbN-based junction can be adopted for SSFQ as well as merged-element transmon with the relatively large junctions. The results presented in this work will offer a new choice of the scalable qubits as well as the material platform toward the realization of large-scale superconducting quantum computers.

item.title: A programmable quantum photonic platform integrating coherent emitters
item.description:
Pay dirt new result — Monolithic GaAs circuit simultaneously operates two individually tunable p-i-n InAs quantum dots and a cryogenic NEMS optical router, achieving g(2)(0)=(0.62±0.07)% and raw two-photon interference visibility of VHOM=(62.2±6.7)%.

Grade 0.468 · 2.5σ above the day's baseline · matched “Semiconductor spin qubits” · Hanna Salamon, Mikkel T. Mikkelsen, Zhe Liu, Peter Lodahl, Severin Krüger, Arne Ludwig, Leonardo Midolo

Figure

(a) Resonance fluorescence spectrum (linewidth ΓRF=351.8±28.0 MHz) and decay rate (̳γ= 1.55±0.08ns⁻¹). (c) Two-photon interference correlation counts versus time delay showing VHOM=(62.2±6.7)% across parallel and perpendicular polarizations at a 50:50 NEMS router setting.

Asks

Can coherent, individually tunable quantum-dot emitters be monolithically integrated with programmable, cryogenic-compatible photonic routing elements on a single chip?

But

Measurements performed at approximately 5 K in a closed-cycle cryostat. Laser leakage and finite frequency scan steps degraded resonance fluorescence HOM visibility and scattering extinction.

Tools

GaAs p-i-n membrane platform · InAs self-assembled quantum dots · NEMS directional coupler router · Photonic crystal waveguides · Superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors (SNSPDs)

Abstract

Photonic quantum technologies require the integration of high-quality quantum light sources with programmable photonic circuitry to enable on-chip quantum information processing. Semiconductor quantum dots have emerged as a leading platform for quantum light generation, yet their monolithic integration with cryogenic-compatible, programmable photonic circuitry remains challenging. Here we demonstrate a programmable quantum photonic platform that enables simultaneous control of highly coherent quantum dot-based single photon emitters and reconfigurable optical elements at cryogenic temperatures. System-level integration enables individual electrical and optical addressing of active components on a single chip, allowing their concurrent operation while preserving coherent non-classical light emission. We demonstrate multiple quantum-photonic functionalities, including pure single-photon generation, two-photon interference, and resonant transmission and reflection measurements of integrated emitters. These results mark a step from isolated quantum-optical devices towards programmable quantum-photonic hardware platforms capable of combining coherent quantum emitters with large-scale photonic functionality.

item.title: Arbitrary-phase CZ gate and remote readout across spatially separated superconducting nodes
item.description:
Pay dirt new method — Realized deterministic arbitrary-phase CZ gate and single-shot readout across superconducting nodes separated by 30 m via bidirectional itinerant photon transfer, reaching maximum bidirectional transfer efficiency of 67%.

Grade 0.466 · 2.5σ above the day's baseline · matched “Cavity quantum electrodynamics for superconducting electrical circuits: An arch…” · Anatoly Kulikov, Josua D. Schär, Alonso Hernández-Antón, Aleksandr Grigorev

Figure

Reconstructed two-qubit density matrices for initial state |++⟩ across varying photon detunings δω=−5 MHz, 0, and 5 MHz, illustrating conditional phase tuning between nodes separated by 30 m.

Asks

Can a complete set of deterministic entangling operations and single-shot qubit readout be executed between spatially separated superconducting quantum nodes without active synchronization or classical communication?

Before

Unidirectional state transfer efficiency between nodes was 84.5% (Kurpiers 2018 / Magnard 2020).

But

Channel attenuation below 1 dB/km at < 60 mK; bidirectional efficiency constrained to 67% due to insertion losses across microwave adapters and connectors traversed twice.

Tools

30-m cryogenic superconducting waveguide link · frequency-tunable transmon qubits · time-reversed sideband Raman emission and absorption · dispersive cavity reflection phase shift

Abstract

Establishing a complete set of gates across spatially separated quantum nodes is fundamental for distributed quantum computation and communication networks. One of the approaches to do so consists of employing a superconducting device as a universal quantum node that is capable of storing and processing quantum information, and traveling microwave photons as means of communication. In this work, we realize an entangling gate across a primitive two-node superconducting circuit QED network consisting of two dilution cryostats, A and B, connected via a 30-m-long cryogenic quantum link. We perform a bidirectional photon transfer protocol, where a microwave photon emitted by the communication qubit at A acquires a conditional phase based on the state of qubit B. We vary the communication photon frequency, hence tuning the conditional phase acquired during the reflection off the remote node, effectively implementing an arbitrary-phase CZ gate. We use this entangling operation to perform single-shot readout of the qubit in node B from node A. An interesting feature of our scheme is that it does not require precise synchronization of the active node with the remote node; in particular, remote readout can be performed without any active participation by the remote node. These protocols add to the quantum communication toolbox with superconducting circuits and provide a way of realizing basic distributed quantum computing operations.

item.title: Micromagnet engineering for enhanced addressability of donor-cluster arrays in silicon
item.description:
Pay dirt new method — On-chip Co micromagnets provide magnetic field gradients ≥0.45 mT/nm over a lateral range of 231 nm, enabling independent addressability of over 120 phosphorus donor spin qubits under a single antenna.

Grade 0.449 · 2.3σ above the day's baseline · matched “Semiconductor spin qubits” · Hao Wang, Baolong Zhao, Shihang Zhang, Ziliang Jin, Huan Shu, Peihao Huang, Guanyong Wang, Mingchao Duan, Tianluo Pan, Tao Xin, Guangchong Hu, Zhen Tian, Dapeng Yu, Yu He

Asks

How can large arrays of STM-patterned donor-cluster spin qubits in silicon be individually addressed without unmanageable wiring overhead?

Before

Hyperfine coupling randomness and Stark tuning alone limit addressability to roughly 30 qubits across 10 distinguishable clusters.

But

Simulations assume idealized single-domain magnetization; fabricated polycrystalline Co exhibits lower remanent magnetization, multi-domain formation, and local magnetic inhomogeneity.

Tools

Scanning tunneling microscope hydrogen depassivation lithography (STM-HDL) · Micromagnetic simulations · Electron-beam evaporation of Co · Scanning nitrogen-vacancy center microscopy (SNVM)

Abstract

Phosphorus donors in silicon are one of the promising platforms for fault-tolerant quantum computing, owing to their long coherence times and compatibility with complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) technology. However, a key bottleneck for scaling this platform lies in the independent addressability of individual spin qubits. Here, we present a scalable quantum processor architecture that integrates scanning tunneling microscope (STM)-defined phosphorus donor-cluster arrays with on-chip micromagnets. By generating magnetic field gradients, the micromagnets enable a broader addressable frequency range compared to the addressing scheme based solely on variations in hyperfine (HF) interactions, which arise from the randomness of intra-cluster configurations. Through micromagnetic simulations to optimize micromagnet geometry, we demonstrate that these structures are compatible with customized array designs, facilitating the integration of over 120 atomic spin qubits and enabling frequency multiplexing with a single microwave antenna, which greatly reduces the overhead of fan-out addressing lines. This design is further validated via magnetic measurements, which generally align with our micromagnetic simulations. These results establish a critical foundation for the development of scalable silicon quantum computing with atomic qubits.

item.title: Field-free dual superconducting diode via photon-assisted interference
item.description:
Pay dirt new result — Biharmonic microwave driving (f=1.405GHz and 2f=2.810GHz) induces field-free, dual-channel supercurrent and quasiparticle rectification in a symmetric Al/AlOx/Al junction, with diode efficiency ηQP≈1 and phase-tunable polarity.

Grade 0.442 · 2.2σ above the day's baseline · matched “materials-limited loss: two-level systems, interfaces, valley splitting” · Laura Borgongino, Rubén Seoane Souto, José Luis del Olmo, Ramón Aguado, Alessandro Crippa, Francesco Giazotto, Elia Strambini

Figure

Current versus voltage traces and diode efficiency ηQP under biharmonic microwave drive at phases θ=±π/2, showing exponential forward turn-on, reverse current suppression, and comparison against Schottky and Tien-Gordon models.

Asks

Can a single, geometrically symmetric superconducting tunnel junction integrate non-reciprocal rectification across both Cooper-pair and quasiparticle channels without applied magnetic fields?

But

Measured at T≈80mK; quasiparticle isolation tested at Fraunhofer minimum (B=17mT) and zero field; reverse state limited by residual subgap leakage and breakdown at VBD≈100μV.

Tools

Al/AlOx/Al tunnel junction · biharmonic microwave drive · multi-tone photon-assisted tunneling · extended Tien-Gordon theory · modified RSJ circuit model

Abstract

Non-reciprocal transport underpins key functionalities in signal processing and logic; however, conventional semiconductor diodes exhibit reduced performance at sub-Kelvin temperatures. As cryogenic electronics continue to scale, there is increasing demand for diode operation compatible with low-temperature and low-dissipation conditions. This need has driven the development of alternatives to p-n junctions that rely on non-reciprocal electron transport mechanisms efficient in the deep-cryogenic regime. Superconducting devices constitute a natural low-loss platform, yet most existing superconducting diodes are restricted to either Cooper-pair or quasiparticle transport, often requiring complex material stacks, asymmetric geometries, or external magnetic fields. No single, geometrically symmetric junction has yet integrated rectification across both transport channels to achieve vanishing resistance under forward bias and strongly suppressed conduction under reverse bias. Here, we demonstrate a dynamically reconfigurable dual-function superconducting diode based on a conventional Al/AlOx/Al tunnel junction. Via microwave biharmonic driving, we exploit multi-tone photon-assisted tunneling to independently control dissipationless and dissipative transport channels within the same device. Varying the microwave drive amplitude induces a transition from a supercurrent diode to an ideal quasiparticle diode, achieving rectification efficiencies exceeding those of conventional Schottky diodes and contemporary superconducting diodes. We further demonstrate AC signal rectification under both current-bias and voltage-bias configurations. Finally, we implement a proof-of-concept "absolute diode" that combines zero forward resistance with strongly suppressed reverse conduction. This tunable approach provides a versatile building block for low-power cryogenic electronic architectures.

item.title: Gate-tunable large second-order and third-order nonlinear Hall effect in topological insulator BiSbTeSe2
item.description:
Pay dirt new result — Demonstrated gate-tunable second-order and third-order nonlinear Hall effects in dual-gated BiSbTeSe2 devices. Second-order response persists up to room temperature with higher generation efficiency than prior topological insulator systems.

Grade 0.426 · 2.0σ above the day's baseline · matched “Semiconductor spin qubits” · Fengyi Guo, Shuai Zhang, Xiubing Li, Zheng Dai, Congcong Li, Yufan Ju, Ziqi Wang, Cheng Bin, Zhe Ying, Fengqi Song

Asks

Can large, highly gate-tunable second-order and third-order nonlinear Hall effects be realized and electrically controlled in topological insulator BiSbTeSe2 devices?

But

Observed up to room temperature.

Tools

dual-gated BiSbTeSe₂ devices · nonlinear Hall effect measurements · scaling analysis

Abstract

The nonlinear Hall effect (NLHE) holds significant promise for next-generation electronic device applications, and it is essential to explore and engineer a strong and highly tunable NLHE. In this work, we report large second-order and third-order NLHEs in dual-gated BiSbTeSe2 devices. Both the second-order and third-order NLHE are highly gate-tunable. The second-order NLHE exhibits a higher generation efficiency than those reported in previous topological insulator systems, and it can be stably observed up to room temperature. Meanwhile, the generation efficiency of the third-order NLHE is comparable to previously reported values. The scaling analysis indicates that the second-order NLHE is consistent with contributions from skew scattering and a term compatible with either the Berry curvature dipole or side jump, whereas the third-order NLHE is consistent with contributions from the Berry connection polarizability tensor and higher-order skew scattering. Our work establishes a promising experimental platform for the development of NLHE-based devices.

item.title: Probing Quantum Anomalous Hall Transport Under Microwave Irradiation Using a Topological Circulator
item.description:
Worth a look new result — Pump-induced transmission change near an exceptional point (642.3 MHz) is approximately 2× that observed away from the point (551.5 MHz), showing non-monotonic frequency-selective response that vanishes at 4 GHz and 7 GHz pump frequencies.

Grade 0.419 · 1.9σ above the day's baseline · matched “Semiconductor spin qubits” · Athul Ashok, Frank Jin, Nick Du, Luis A. Martinez, Jenny Zhou, Sean O'Kelley, Zachary J. -R. Espley, Gang Qiu, Kang L. Wang, Dong-Xia Qu

Figure

Transmission magnitude |S32| versus continuous-wave pump power across 1 to 9 GHz pump frequencies, compared at probe frequencies of 551.5 MHz and 642.3 MHz (near the exceptional point).

Asks

How does microwave irradiation perturb chiral edge magnetoplasmon transport in a quantum anomalous Hall topological circulator near an exceptional point?

But

Measured at dilution refrigerator temperatures between 50 mK and 300 mK; device uses a specific 100 μm-radius mesa geometry coupled to lumped-element LC resonators.

Tools

quantum anomalous Hall circulator · Cr-doped (Bi,Sb)2Te3 · pump-probe microwave spectroscopy · RFSoC/QICK FPGA platform · dilution refrigerator

Abstract

Edge magnetoplasmons (EMPs) provide a platform for probing chiral charge dynamics and nonreciprocal microwave transport in topological quantum materials. However, detecting small perturbations to EMP propagation remains challenging because their signatures in conventional microwave scattering measurements can be weak. Here, we investigate microwave-photon-induced perturbations of EMP transport using a quantum anomalous Hall topological circulator. Pump--probe measurements reveal a strongly frequency-selective response: while microwave irradiation substantially modifies the EMP transmission at several pump frequencies, the transmission remains nearly unchanged at selected frequencies, including 4 and 7 GHz. We further exploit the non-Hermitian mode hybridization of the coupled EMP-resonator system to probe the response near an exceptional point (EP). The pump-induced change in transmission magnitude near the EP is approximately twice that observed away from the EP, demonstrating an enhanced microwave response to perturbations. These results reveal the interplay among chiral EMP transport, microwave-photon-induced perturbations, and non-Hermitian dynamics, and demonstrate the potential of topological circulators as a promising platform for enhanced microwave spectroscopy and sensing.
